newsitem.title: HONG KONG: One third of Hong Kong favours independence--polls.
newsitem.headline: One third of Hong Kong favours independence--polls.

text.p: Fewer than half of Hong Kong's people support merger with China, and a third favour independence, according to opinion poll results on Thursday.

Some 40 percent believed Hong Kong should join China, while 35 percent would like independence and 19 percent would have preferred Hong Kong to stay a British colony, combined May-June polls in the South China Morning Post newspaper showed. Six percent expressed no opinion.
Britain is handing Hong Kong back to China at midnight next Monday after 156 years of colonial rule.

Most British colonies became independent states after their decolonisation. But Hong Kong was seized from China in 1841 in the Sino-British opium war, and Beijing has always regarded it as sovereign territory.
Advocating independence will become a crime in Hong Kong after the handover because it threatens "national security".

An overview of polls during May and June collated by the Post also showed that if fair and democratic elections were held now for Hong Kong's parliament, the Democratic Party would beat pro-Beijing forces hands down.
The party, led by lawyer Martin Lee, the voice of democacy in Hong Kong, would win 44 percent of the votes, and under a first-past-the-post British-style system Lee would become prime minister.

But China is reversing democratic reforms introduced in Hong Kong over the past five years and replacing the elected Legislative Council with an appointed interim body until elections are held under new rules next year.

David Bottomley, one of Hong Kong's leading pollsters, wrote that if the future government installed by China rigs the next election to handicap the democrats, this would harden the divisions of political opinion in society.
